question.problem: Margaret has $$1,500$ saved. Of this amount, she decides to spend $22.4%$ to buy some supplies for her farm. How much money does Margret plan to spend?
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we can use the formula:

$$
\text{part}=\text{percentage}\times \text{whole}
$$

In our case, the whole is the amount of money Margaret has saved, which is $$1,500.$ The percentage is $22.4%,$ and the part is the amount of money that she decides to spend.

**Method 1**

First, we convert the percentage to a decimal:

$$
22.4%=22.4÷100=0.224
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =22.4%\times 1,500 \\  & =0.224\times 1,500 \\  & =336\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $22.4%$ of $1,500$ is $336.$ Thus, Margaret plans to spend $$336.$

**Method 2**

First, we convert the percentage to a fraction:

$$
22.4%=\frac{22.4}{100}
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =22.4%\times 1,500 \\  & =\frac{22.4}{100}\times 1,500 \\  & =22.4\times \frac{1,500}{100} \\  & =22.4\times 15 \\  & =336\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $22.4%$ of $1,500$ is $336.$ Thus, Margaret plans to spend $$336.$
